name: worktree-coach-chained-git
description: A session isolated in a worktree (claude --worktree) runs `cd src && git log -1 --oneline $(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)`, which Claude Code refuses as too complex to verify. With the mod on, Claude reads the note (Claude Code's reason and remedy, the worktree path, fixed tips; nothing of the command) and recovers with git -C; with it off, the refusal arrives without a note.

sessions.name: mod on
sessions.prompt:
Run exactly this Bash command, unchanged, as your first tool call: cd src && git log -1 --oneline $(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
If it is refused, follow the guidance that comes with the refusal to get that log line, then reply with one line saying what you ran.

assert.matches: This session is isolated in the worktree .*too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree
assert.label: Claude Code refused the chained git command

assert.matches: worktree-coach: Claude Code refused this command because \\"this command names git in a form too complex to verify
assert.label: the note reached the model, quoting Claude Code's reason

assert.matches: Your worktree: [^ ]*coach-on\\n- Run each git command as its own Bash call\.\\n- Use `git -C [^`]*coach-on` with exactly this path\.
assert.label: the note gives the worktree path and the fixed tips

assert.notMatches: worktree-coach: Claude Code refused(?:(?!Do not resend).)*(rev-parse|abbrev-ref|--oneline|cd src)
assert.label: the note echoes nothing of the refused command

sessions.name: mod off
sessions.prompt:
Run exactly this Bash command, unchanged, as your only tool call: cd src && git log -1 --oneline $(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
Then reply with one line saying whether it ran.

assert.matches: too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree
assert.label: Claude Code refused the chained git command
